name: sudokumaker-mcp

tools.name: initiate_session
tools.description: Initiate a browser automation session. Shows an approval dialog to the user with the session code. Returns a session token and extension connection ID on approval, or indicates rejection.

sessionCode.description: A short, readable code shown to the user in the approval dialog to confirm the session is legitimate

tools.name: list_tabs
tools.description: List all open browser tabs

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabProps.description: Which tab properties to return in the response. Please specify as few fields as possible that are enough to achieve your goal, in order to save the traffic.

tools.name: docs
tools.description:
Fetch a documentation topic by name.
Start every session with the `intro` topic.

topic.description:
The documentation topic to fetch.
Omit to get the index of available topics.

tools.name: get_puzzle
tools.description: Read the puzzle object for the target tab, formatted for reading, or one nested value inside it via `path`.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

path.description:
Dot-joined handle to a nested value inside the puzzle (e.g. `"allElements.3.config.style"`), copied
from a handle printed in a previous `get_puzzle` call or a mutation echo. Grid nodes take cell
notation (`"cells.r2c3"`, `"cells.r2"`).

Omit to read the entire puzzle. Narrow with `path` whenever you already know which part you need -
it returns only that sub-value instead of the whole puzzle, which is cheaper for a large puzzle.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description:
Read the app's own solver log (deductions, solve results, validity check results) as plain text, one
entry per line, oldest first. This is the same log the solver tools (`logical_step`,
`all_logical_steps`, `brute_force_solve`, `check_validity`) already report
their new entries from - use this tool instead when older entries are needed, or when a solver action
was triggered outside this session.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

json.description: Return the raw log entries as JSON instead of the formatted text.

tools.name: update_puzzle_metadata
tools.description:
Change the puzzle's title, author, rules text, completion message, or digit range.
Every field is optional - skip whatever you're not changing.

This tool does not cover the puzzle's grid dimensions or its type (sudoku/custom) - changing either is not supported by any tool by design.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

operationDescription.description: Plain-language sentence describing what this call will actually change, for the user to approve or reject.

name.description: Puzzle title, shown to the solver.

author.description: Puzzle author/setter name, shown to the solver.

comment.description: Rules text, shown to the solver. Usually describes the puzzle's rules, but can hold any text.

content.description: The new complete text, replacing whatever it held before.

old_string.description: Exact text to find and replace.

new_string.description: Text to put in place of `old_string`.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of just one.

edit.description: Finds `old_string` and replaces it with `new_string`. `old_string` must match exactly one location, unless `replace_all` is set.

content.description: Text to add after the current content.
Text to add before the current content.

completionMessage.description: Message shown to the solver after they successfully complete the puzzle. Pass an empty string to remove it.

minDigit.description: Lowest digit allowed in the grid (e.g. 1 for standard sudoku, 0 for a 0-indexed variant).

maxDigit.description: Highest digit allowed in the grid (e.g. 9 for standard sudoku).

tools.name: update_given_digits
tools.description:
Set or clear the given digits in one or more grid cells.

Setting a given digit also clears any candidates/corner marks already in that cell.
Marking a cell as given wipes any solver-entered value there and replaces it with the given digit.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

items.description: A cell coordinate string in "rXcY" notation, e.g. "r2c3" is row 2, column 3 (both 1-based, counting from the top-left). Row/column may be 0 or negative, or greater than the grid size, for cells outside the grid.

digit.description: The given digit to place in each target cell, or `-1` to remove the given digit from each target cell.

tools.name: update_cell_values
tools.description:
Set or clear the solver-entered value (a hand-entered digit, not a given/fixed clue)
in one or more grid cells - what a human solver would type in while solving.

To change given digits instead, use `update_given_digits`.

Setting a value also clears any candidates/corner marks already in that cell.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

items.description: A cell coordinate string in "rXcY" notation, e.g. "r2c3" is row 2, column 3 (both 1-based, counting from the top-left). Row/column may be 0 or negative, or greater than the grid size, for cells outside the grid.

digit.description: The digit to place in each target cell, or `-1` to clear the cell's value.

tools.name: update_cell_marks
tools.description:
Add, replace, or remove pencil marks and/or cell colors in one or more grid cells:
candidates (center marks), corner pencil marks, and cell background colors.

A solved cell has no pencil marks, so candidates/`cornerPencilMarks` changes don't apply to cells
that already contain a value; colors can still be applied to such cells.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

operationDescription.description: Plain-language sentence describing what this call will actually change, for the user to approve or reject.

items.description: A cell coordinate string in "rXcY" notation, e.g. "r2c3" is row 2, column 3 (both 1-based, counting from the top-left). Row/column may be 0 or negative, or greater than the grid size, for cells outside the grid.

operation.description:
How to combine the given values with each cell's existing marks:

- `"add"` unions them in.
- `"replace"` overwrites the mark list outright (use an empty array to clear all marks of a kind).
- `"remove"` subtracts them out.

candidates.description:
Set of possible candidates for the cell.
        Omit to leave candidates untouched.

cornerPencilMarks.description:
Digits marked in the corners of the cell. The meaning of the corner marks is subjective and free to interpretation.
          
          Omit to leave corner marks untouched.

colors.description:
Background colors of the cell. The meaning of colors depends on context: sometimes marking a set of cells with the same color means that these cells have the same digit or the same set of digits, sometimes colors are purely cosmetic, sometimes it's something else. Mixing a color together with white usually means that whatever is associated with the non-white color could go in one of the cells marked with this color and white.
        
        Omit to leave colors untouched.

tools.name: add_element
tools.description:
Create a new element (a constraint or a decorative/cosmetic element) in the puzzle and insert it
into the element list at a chosen position.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

name.description: Element name. Leave it empty to use the default (recommended when there is only one element of the type).

enabled.description: Is the element enabled? Disabling an element will hide its visual clues from the grid and exclude its logic from the solver, which is the same as if the element doesn't exist. Useful to temporarily exclude the element from the puzzle without deleting it from the list.

solverIgnored.description: Ignore the element's logic in the solver while still showing the visuals in the grid. Use it to make element cosmetic-only, or if you want to temporarily ignore its logic.

type.description: The exact element type name to create, e.g. `"KillerCages"`, `"Thermometer"`, `"CosmeticSymbol"` - browse valid type names in docs topic `elements`.

subType.description: The exact title of one of that type's variants - docs topic `element:<TypeName>`'s `## Variants` section lists them.

params.description: Only for subtypes that need them: subtype-specific creation parameters, shape given alongside the variant in `## Variants` when it takes one.

overrides.description:
Only for types with a `## Config` section: initial config values to set instead of the type's defaults (e.g. `{"style": {"color": "#ff0000"}}`) -
docs topic `element:<TypeName>`'s `## Config` section shows the full config JSON schema.

Send only the fields you want to change, at any nesting level - any field you omit (at any level) keeps its current value. If you include an array-valued field, it replaces the whole array rather than merging item-by-item.

element.description:
Which type/variant of element to create and its initial config.

The new element's clue list (for multi-clue types) always starts empty regardless of `overrides` -
use `add_clues` afterwards.

Example: `{"type": "Thermometer", "subType": "Thermometer", "overrides": {"style": {"color": "#888888"}}}`.

at.description: The 1-based position to insert at, e.g. `1` to place it as the first item.

anyOf.description: Place the new element at the Nth position.
Insert the new element at the end of the list.

elementId.description: Target element ID. This is the element's ID, not its `allElements.N` handle - the handle shifts if elements are reordered, the ID doesn't.

anyOf.description: Place the new element immediately before or after another element with the given ID.

position.description: Where to insert the new element in the puzzle's ordered element list (order affects layering).

tools.name: update_element
tools.description:
Update an existing element's own fields, and/or batch-apply the same partial update to every one
of its clues at once.

To update individual clues differently from each other, use `update_clues` instead -
the `clueBatchUpdates` field here applies identically to ALL clues.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

elementId.description:
ID of the target element to update, as returned by `get_puzzle`/`add_element`.
This is the element's ID, not its `allElements.N` handle - the handle shifts if elements are reordered, the ID doesn't.

operationDescription.description: Plain-language sentence describing what this call will actually change, for the user to approve or reject.

elementUpdates.description:
Object of the element's config fields to change (e.g. `{"style": {"bulbRadius": 0.6}}` for a
thermometer) - only accepted for element types that have config beyond their clues; docs topic
`element:<TypeName>`'s `## Config` section shows the full config JSON schema.

Send only the fields you want to change, at any nesting level - any field you omit (at any level) keeps its current value. If you include an array-valued field, it replaces the whole array rather than merging item-by-item.
To unset an optional field rather than give it a new value, send `null` for it.

clueBatchUpdates.description:
Object applied identically to every clue this element currently has (e.g. `{"value": 0}` would
zero every cage's total) - only accepted for multi-clue element types; docs topic
`element:<TypeName>`'s `## Clues` section shows the exact clue JSON schema.

Send only the fields you want to change, at any nesting level - any field you omit (at any level) keeps its current value. If you include an array-valued field, it replaces the whole array rather than merging item-by-item.
To unset an optional field rather than give it a new value, send `null` for it.

name.description: Rename the element (skip to leave the current name, pass an empty string to revert to the default name).

enabled.description: Enable or disable the element (both logic and visuals).

solverIgnored.description: Enable or disable the element for the solver (logic only).

tools.name: remove_element
tools.description: Delete an entire element (and all of its clues, if any) from the puzzle by ID.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

elementId.description:
ID of the element to remove, as returned by `get_puzzle`/`add_element`.
This is the element's ID, not its `allElements.N` handle - the handle shifts if elements are reordered, the ID doesn't.

elementName.description: The element's display name - set it so the user sees which element they're deleting when reviewing this call, not just a bare ID.

tools.name: add_clues
tools.description:
Append one or more clues to an existing multi-clue element (e.g. add thermometers to a
`Thermometer` element, or arrows to an `Arrow` element). The
clues are pushed onto the end of the element's clue list; use
`update_clues`/`remove_clues` to change or delete existing ones.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

elementId.description:
ID of the target element (the multi-clue element to add clues to), as returned by `get_puzzle`/`add_element`.
This is the element's ID, not its `allElements.N` handle - the handle shifts if elements are reordered, the ID doesn't.

operationDescription.description: Plain-language sentence describing what this call will actually change, for the user to approve or reject.

clues.description:
Array of new clues to append to the element's clue list, one array entry per new clue; docs topic
`element:<TypeName>` (substitute the target element's exact type name, e.g.
`element:Thermometer`)'s `## Clues` section shows the exact clue JSON schema.

Example (for a `Thermometer` element): `[["r1c1", "r1c2", "r1c3"]]`.

tools.name: update_clues
tools.description:
Update one or more existing clues of a multi-clue element (e.g. retotal killer cages, retarget an arrow).

The response lists which clues each group matched - **undo immediately** if a match wasn't the clue
you intended.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

elementId.description:
ID of the target element (the multi-clue element whose clues to update), as returned by `get_puzzle`/`add_element`.
This is the element's ID, not its `allElements.N` handle - the handle shifts if elements are reordered, the ID doesn't.

operationDescription.description: Plain-language sentence describing what this call will actually change, for the user to approve or reject.

items.description: A cell coordinate string in "rXcY" notation, e.g. "r2c3" is row 2, column 3 (both 1-based, counting from the top-left). Row/column may be 0 or negative, or greater than the grid size, for cells outside the grid.

clueCells.description:
A group of cells that identifies which clue(s) to target.
A clue matches only if **all** cells in the group are among the cells it affects.

Pass enough cells to identify one clue uniquely, or fewer to target several clues at once.

positions.description: 1-based positions in the element's clue array, selecting exactly those clues.

match.description: Selects which clue(s) of an element to target, by cell group or by position.

updates.description:
An update for the clue: usually an object holding only the fields to change, but a clue whose whole
shape is a single string or array (e.g. a thermometer's cell list) takes that value directly instead
of an object. Docs topic `element:<TypeName>` (substitute the target element's exact type name,
e.g. `element:KillerCages`)'s `## Clues` section shows the exact
clue JSON schema.

Send only the fields you want to change, at any nesting level - any field you omit (at any level) keeps its current value. If you include an array-valued field, it replaces the whole array rather than merging item-by-item.
To unset an optional field rather than give it a new value, send `null` for it.

updateGroups.description:
Array of group objects. Every clue matched by a group's `match` receives that same group's `updates` object.

Example: `[{"match": {"clueCells": ["r1c1"]}, "updates": {"value": 21}}]`.

tools.name: remove_clues
tools.description:
Delete one or more existing clues of a multi-clue element (e.g. remove a `Thermometer`,
delete an `Arrow`).

The response lists which clues were matched and removed - **undo immediately** if a match wasn't
the clue you intended.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

elementId.description:
ID of the target element (the multi-clue element to remove clues from), as returned by `get_puzzle`/`add_element`.
This is the element's ID, not its `allElements.N` handle - the handle shifts if elements are reordered, the ID doesn't.

operationDescription.description: Plain-language sentence describing what this call will actually change, for the user to approve or reject.

positions.description: 1-based positions in the element's clue array, selecting exactly those clues.

items.description: A cell coordinate string in "rXcY" notation, e.g. "r2c3" is row 2, column 3 (both 1-based, counting from the top-left). Row/column may be 0 or negative, or greater than the grid size, for cells outside the grid.

A group of cells that identifies which clue(s) to target.
A clue matches only if **all** cells in the group are among the cells it affects.

Pass enough cells to identify one clue uniquely, or fewer to target several clues at once.

match.description:
Which clues to remove: either `positions` to remove exact clues directly, or `clueCellGroups` -
one or more cell groups, each independently selecting the clue(s) it matches.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Revert the last action taken in the puzzle - whether it was made by this MCP server or by the user directly in the app's UI.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Re-apply the last action that was undone (via `undo` or directly in the app's UI).

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: clear_grid
tools.description:
Clear all non-given digits and markings (values, candidates, corner marks, colors) from every grid
cell, leaving given digits untouched.

Note: this action could be undone and redone by calling "undo" and "redo" tools, similar to any other action in the puzzle

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: logical_step
tools.description:
Run one round of human-style logical deduction and write any newly deduced candidates/eliminations
into the grid's center marks (overwriting existing center marks).

Blind to free-text rules and cosmetic-only elements; may miss deductions `brute_force_solve` would find.

Note: this action could be undone and redone by calling "undo" and "redo" tools, similar to any other action in the puzzle

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: all_logical_steps
tools.description:
Repeatedly run human-style logical deduction until no further step is found, writing all deduced
candidates/eliminations into the grid's center marks (overwriting existing center marks).

Blind to free-text rules and cosmetic-only elements; may leave the puzzle unsolved even when
`brute_force_solve` would succeed.

Note: this action could be undone and redone by calling "undo" and "redo" tools, similar to any other action in the puzzle - all steps taken in this call are undone/redone together as one action.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: brute_force_solve
tools.description:
Exhaustively search for every solution consistent with the current givens, entered values, and
marks; fills in digits if the solution is unique, and always writes the exact valid candidates into
center marks (overwriting existing center marks).

This is the only reliable way to know the puzzle's solution count and the exact valid candidates
for every cell - `logical_step`/`all_logical_steps` only deduce what a human-style pass finds and
may miss eliminations or leave the puzzle unsolved even when this tool would succeed.

Blind to free-text rules and cosmetic-only elements. Search is capped - a very high solution count
may be reported as "stopped counting" rather than an exact number.

Note: this action could be undone and redone by calling "undo" and "redo" tools, similar to any other action in the puzzle

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: check_validity
tools.description:
Run the app's own existence-and-uniqueness check and report its verdict: whether the puzzle has a
solution at all, and if so, whether it's unique. Writes nothing to the grid - unlike
`brute_force_solve`, this is safe to run at any time without disturbing existing values or marks.

Already-entered cell values and center marks are treated as constraints, so a verdict is conditional
on them when present.

Blind to free-text rules and cosmetic-only elements.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: wait_for_solver
tools.description:
Block until the currently running solver operation (`logical_step`, `all_logical_steps`,
`brute_force_solve`, or `check_validity`) finishes, then return its result.

Use this if a previous solver call's response indicated the solve was still in progress.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)

tools.name: stop_solver
tools.description: Abort a currently running solver operation before it finishes on its own.

extensionConnectionId.description: Extension connection ID obtained from initiate_session

tabId.description: ID of the browser tab to target (from list_tabs)
